title: Predictive Analytics and AI in Revenue Cycle
summary: AI and machine learning are moving RCM from reactive to predictive — identifying denial risk, optimizing work queues, and automating routine billing tasks.
objectives: Describe the AI applications currently deployed in revenue cycle management
Explain how predictive denial management works and its ROI
Identify the risks and limitations of AI-driven RCM automation

content_blocks.body:
Artificial intelligence is being applied across the revenue cycle:

- **Prior authorization automation:** AI predicts which cases require PA and auto-submits requests, reducing manual burden
- **Predictive denial scoring:** ML models score each claim pre-submission with a denial probability, allowing targeted intervention before submission
- **Autonomous coding:** NLP-based tools read clinical documentation and suggest ICD-10 and CPT codes for human review
- **Intelligent work queue management:** AI prioritizes AR follow-up by expected recovery value rather than dollar amount alone
- **Payment prediction:** Models predict when each claim will pay and flag claims deviating from predicted payment patterns
- **Robotic Process Automation (RPA):** Bots handle repetitive tasks like eligibility checks, claim status inquiries, and payment posting

content_blocks.body: AI in RCM carries risks: (1) Predictive models trained on historical data may perpetuate existing billing biases, under-prioritizing claims from low-reimbursement payers; (2) NLP coding tools can 'hallucinate' codes not supported by documentation, creating compliance risk; (3) Payer AI denial systems may flag human-reviewed claims as 'not medically necessary' based on criteria that differ from clinical judgment. Maintain human oversight for all AI-generated coding and clinical necessity determinations.
